description: ECDAT Context-Aware Post-Quantum Cryptography and Classical Remediation Recommendations

recommendations.current_condition: TLS session utilizing classical key agreement (ECDHE/DHE) or static RSA key exchange.
recommendations.proposed_option: Enable TLS 1.3 with X25519MLKEM768 (or SecP256r1MLKEM768) hybrid key exchange group.
recommendations.security_rationale: X25519MLKEM768 provides 128-bit classical security via Curve25519 ECDHE and NIST Security Category 3 quantum security via ML-KEM-768 lattice-based key encapsulation. The combiner function ensures IND-CCA2 security holds if either underlying assumption (Discrete Logarithm or Module-LWE) remains hard, actively neutralizing HNDL threats.
recommendations.confidence_and_assumptions: Assumes modern TLS stack (OpenSSL 3.2+, BoringSSL, Go 1.23+, or Cloudflare/AWS edge proxies) that supports hybrid post-quantum key shares in the TLS ClientHello.

recommendations.current_condition: Custom or protocol-level key encapsulation/establishment using classical RSA-OAEP or ECDH.
recommendations.proposed_option: Migrate to ML-KEM-768 (NIST Security Category 3) or ML-KEM-1024 (Category 5) in a dual-KEM hybrid envelope.
recommendations.standard_reference: NIST FIPS 203 & RFC 9180 (HPKE with PQC extension)
recommendations.security_rationale: Shor's algorithm solves both the discrete logarithm (DLP) and integer factorization (IFP) problems in polynomial time O((log N)^3) on a CRQC, completely breaking RSA/ECC. ML-KEM provides semantic security under chosen ciphertext attack (IND-CCA2) based on the computational hardness of the Module Learning with Errors (M-LWE) problem.
recommendations.confidence_and_assumptions: ML-KEM public keys (~1184 bytes) and ciphertexts (~1088 bytes) are larger than classical EC keys (~32-64 bytes). Ensure buffers and database fields accommodate expanded payloads.

recommendations.current_condition: Digital signature verification and generation using classical RSA, DSA, or ECDSA.
recommendations.proposed_option: Migrate to ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) for general signatures, or SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) where stateless hash assumptions are preferred.
recommendations.security_rationale: A CRQC executing Shor's algorithm can recover classical RSA/ECC private keys from public keys in polynomial time, enabling trivial signature forgery. ML-DSA (FIPS 204) provides EUF-CMA security derived from the hardness of the Module Short Integer Solution (M-SIS) and M-LWE problems.
recommendations.confidence_and_assumptions: Signature size increases from ~64 bytes (ECDSA) to ~3.3 KB (ML-DSA-65) or ~17 KB (SLH-DSA). X.509 PKI certificates and verification caches must support larger certificate chains.

recommendations.current_condition: Firmware verification, bootloader integrity, or constrained device code signing with strictly bounded signature counts.
recommendations.proposed_option: Implement stateful hash-based signatures (LMS/HSS via RFC 8554 or XMSS via RFC 8391).
recommendations.standard_reference: NIST SP 800-208 & CNSA 2.0 Timeline for Software/Firmware Signing
recommendations.security_rationale: LMS/HSS and XMSS rely purely on the pre-image and collision resistance of the underlying cryptographic hash function (e.g., SHA-256). They do not depend on number-theoretic assumptions, offering conservative post-quantum security under the condition that state (Merkle tree leaf index) is monotonically incremented on NVRAM.
recommendations.confidence_and_assumptions: Requires state management across signing operations to prevent one-time key reuse catastrophic security failures. Verification is stateless and extremely fast.

recommendations.current_condition: SSH server or client utilizing classical diffie-hellman-group-exchange or ecdh-sha2-nistp256.
recommendations.proposed_option: Configure SSH to negotiate sntrup761x25519-sha512@openssh.com or mlkem768x25519-sha512@openssh.com.
recommendations.security_rationale: Standard SSH KEX (e.g., diffie-hellman-group14-sha256) is susceptible to retrospective decryption. `sntrup761x25519-sha512` provides a composite KEM leveraging the hardness of the NTRU lattice problem alongside classical Curve25519 ECDH to secure the session key material.
recommendations.confidence_and_assumptions: Supported by default in OpenSSH 9.0 and later. Ensure legacy embedded or bastion devices support the hybrid key exchange algorithms.

recommendations.current_condition: Long-lived encrypted data (shelf-life > 10 years, e.g. financial ledgers, medical records, backups) protected by classical RSA/ECDH key wraps.
recommendations.proposed_option: Wrap symmetric data encryption keys (DEKs) using a hybrid KEM (ML-KEM-768 + X25519) and re-encrypt DEKs under AES-256-GCM.
recommendations.standard_reference: CNSA 2.0 Stored Data Guidance & NIST FIPS 203
recommendations.security_rationale: To neutralize HNDL on ciphertext with a shelf-life X > Z (quantum threat horizon), Data Encryption Keys (DEKs) wrapped via classical RSA-OAEP must be re-wrapped using a dual-KEM envelope (e.g., RSA-3072 + ML-KEM-768). The underlying block cipher must also utilize a 256-bit key space to maintain a 128-bit quantum security margin against Grover's algorithm.
recommendations.confidence_and_assumptions: Requires envelope re-wrapping and key management system (KMS) support for PQC key types. Existing symmetric ciphertext does not need full bulk re-encryption if the DEK is sufficiently long (AES-256).

recommendations.current_condition: Symmetric encryption using AES-128 for high-value or long-retention data.
recommendations.proposed_option: Upgrade to AES-256 in Galois/Counter Mode (AES-256-GCM) or ChaCha20-Poly1305.
recommendations.standard_reference: NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev 5 & CNSA 2.0 Symmetric Cipher Mandate
recommendations.security_rationale: Grover's amplitude amplification algorithm accelerates unstructured exhaustive key search to O(sqrt(N)), reducing the effective quantum security margin of AES-128 to ~64 bits. AES-256 is mandated to ensure a post-quantum minimum of 128 bits of symmetric entropy.
recommendations.confidence_and_assumptions: Hardware AES-NI acceleration in x86/ARM processors handles AES-256 with negligible performance penalty (typically < 10% CPU overhead over AES-128).

recommendations.current_condition: Usage of deprecated cryptographic hash functions MD5 or SHA-1.
recommendations.proposed_option: Replace with SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-3 (FIPS 202). For password storage, migrate to Argon2id (RFC 9106).
recommendations.security_rationale: MD5 and SHA-1 exhibit catastrophic vulnerability to differential collision attacks (O(2^18) and O(2^61) complexity, respectively). Migration to SHA-256 or SHA-3 provides classical collision resistance bounds of O(2^(n/2)) and sufficient pre-image resistance bounds of O(2^n) against both classical and quantum adversaries.
recommendations.confidence_and_assumptions: Digest sizes change from 128/160 bits to 256+ bits. Ensure database schema and protocol fields accommodate expanded hash outputs.

recommendations.current_condition: X.509 Certificate utilizing classical RSA or ECDSA public keys for identity or mTLS authentication.
recommendations.proposed_option: Maintain at least RSA-3072 or ECDSA P-256 during transition, while preparing dual-signature / composite PQC certificates with ML-DSA-65 or SLH-DSA.
recommendations.security_rationale: X.509 PKI chains relying on classical EC/RSA digital signatures will fail to provide non-repudiation and entity authentication against a CRQC. Composite certificates embed both a classical (e.g., ECDSA P-256) and PQC (e.g., ML-DSA-65) SubjectPublicKeyInfo (SPKI) and signature, ensuring OID parsing compatibility while establishing EUF-CMA post-quantum trust.
recommendations.confidence_and_assumptions: Requires CA/Browser Forum and OS trust store ecosystem support for PQC root certificates.

recommendations.current_condition: Hardcoded cryptographic key material discovered in static source code or configuration artifacts.
recommendations.proposed_option: Immediately revoke and purge embedded key material from repository history; rotate to a secure KMS/HSM and issue hybrid keypairs.
recommendations.standard_reference: NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 & OWASP Key Management Cheat Sheet
recommendations.security_rationale: Hardcoded key material in compiled artifacts violates CWE-798, allowing deterministic recovery of secret parameters via reverse-engineering (e.g., strings or entropy analysis). Key custody must be transferred to a FIPS 140-3 Level 3 HSM or KMS using envelope encryption.
recommendations.confidence_and_assumptions: Key rotation can be performed immediately in KMS without rewriting client application logic.

recommendations.current_condition: Cryptographic library dependency identified in binary, container, or package inventory.
recommendations.proposed_option: Upgrade to library versions featuring native post-quantum or hybrid algorithm support (e.g. OpenSSL 3.2+, wolfSSL with liboqs, Go 1.23+).
recommendations.standard_reference: CNSA 2.0 Software Ecosystem Roadmap & OQS Project
recommendations.security_rationale: Legacy cryptographic providers lack OID mappings and algorithmic support for lattice-based mechanisms. Upgrading to OpenSSL 3.2+ or wolfSSL with liboqs integration exposes standardized EVP APIs for ML-KEM/ML-DSA, satisfying FIPS 140-3 boundaries and CNSA 2.0 timelines.
recommendations.confidence_and_assumptions: Library presence indicates capability; active runtime invocation must be confirmed via AST or network discovery.
